subject: System Design
title: Distributed Locks
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Distributed Locks.

hook.text: Two workers process the same payment. Without a distributed lock, the customer is charged twice.

buildup.text: A distributed lock ensures only one process can access a resource across multiple machines.

discovery.text: Redis and ZooKeeper provide lock primitives. Redlock uses multiple Redis instances for safer locking.

twist.text: Distributed locks can fail: clock skew, GC pauses, or network delays can cause two processes to hold the same lock.

climax.text: Distributed locks are necessary but imperfect. Idempotent operations are safer than relying on locks alone.

punchline.text: Locks prevent double-processing — but are never perfect.

quiz.question: Why can distributed locks fail?
options: Clock skew, GC pauses, or network delays can invalidate locks
They only work on one machine
